newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Volvo Trucks seen making U.S. purchase.
newsitem.headline: Volvo Trucks seen making U.S. purchase.

text.p: Volvo Trucks is seeking to acquire a rival on the North American market in its bid for world leadership in heavy truck production, analysts said on Friday.
They said the truckmaker is analysing possible candidates for a takeover, and most fingers point to Mack Trucks, which is owned by Renault.
"They are most certainly looking to buy something in the North American market," said Hans Westerberg, analyst at Den Danske Bank (DDB).
"Karl-Erling Trogen (CEO of Volvo Trucks) has clearly spelled out that an acquisition is in order to strengthen the company's market position in North America," he added.
Volvo Trucks declined to comment in detail on Friday.

"There is currently restructuring going on in the truck production industry and Volvo Trucks is of course playing a part in that," spokesman Stefan Lorentzson told Reuters. "Internally, we work with a lot of different scenarios but of course we won't give detailed comment about them."

But Volvo Group CEO Leif Johansson has not ruled out the possibility of a North American acquisition, and his stated intention is for Volvo Trucks to become the leading heavy truck producer worldwide by 2005.

"Johansson has pointed out that an acquisition of some sort is on its way and that it will be significant," said John Lawson, analyst at Salomon Brothers in London. "I still think, however, that he will want to wait a couple of quarters after his recent appointment before he is ready to close a big deal."
Analysts say North America is a target for Volvo because its trucks arm is not, in the longer term, large enough to cope alone there.
A purchase in America would give Volvo access to a wider sales and distribution network, which would enable it to grow downstream in an important and profitable market.

"In the long run, Volvo Trucks isn't large enough in North America," said Lawson. "The problem is, however, that there are no truck producers to buy. Before a deal can be signed I think that Volvo Truck would have to prove itself by showing black figures once more."
Although Mack is seen as the most likely candidate, other possible targets include Paccar and Navistar, analysts said.
"The most probably acquisistion is Mack. But it's all down to timing..whichever board of directors decides to leave the heavy truck market in North America next," DDB's Hans Westerberg said.
One possible outcome is that Renault negotiates a partnership deal with the Swedish truckmaker.

"I doubt whether Renault will sell Mack on its own. What might happen is that it looks to find a partnership solution for its European truck operation, and sells Mack in that package," Philippe Barrier, analyst at Societe Generale in Paris told Reuters.
